presentation.title: Verification and Modelling of Tsunami Arrival Time and Wave Height Along Thailand's Andaman Sea Coast Using an Enhanced TOAST (O5.1-327)

profile.current_position: Research Scientist, Seismology and Tsunami Monitoring Division
profile.research_focus: Tsunami modeling and verification, coastal hazard assessment, enhanced TOAST (Tsunami Observation and Simulation Terminal) modeling systems
profile.geographic_focus: Thailand's Andaman Sea coast, with particular expertise in the region affected by the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami
profile.research_impact: Develops and validates enhanced tsunami modeling systems to improve early warning capabilities and coastal disaster preparedness for Thailand's vulnerable Andaman Sea coastline
profile.institutional_context: Likely affiliated with Thai disaster management or oceanographic research institutions focused on tsunami risk reduction
profile.relevance_to_ctbto: Tsunami modeling expertise relates to hydroacoustic monitoring applications and understanding of ocean-atmosphere interactions relevant to comprehensive monitoring systems
profile.key_research_project: Enhancement of the TOAST (Tsunami Observation and Simulation Terminal) model by increasing bathymetry resolution from 3.7 km to 0.46 km and refining coastal impact analysis to the subdistrict level, improving forecast accuracy for the Andaman Sea region.
profile.validation_methodology: Comparison of enhanced TOAST model simulations of the 2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami against tidal gauge records from multiple coastal stations, verifying first wave and maximum wave arrival times.
key_findings: First wave arrival predictions matched tidal gauge data within a 0-5 minute margin.
Maximum wave arrival deviations were quantified as 9 minutes early at Kuraburi and 28 minutes late at Taphao Noi.
Lam Kaen Subdistrict identified as the first impacted region; Thung Maphrao Subdistrict experienced the highest wave heights.
profile.disaster_management_collaboration: Research outputs are integrated into TMD’s tsunami early warning bulletins, which are disseminated in coordination with Thailand’s National Disaster Warning Center (NDWC) and the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation (DDPM).
